newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen off in late trade despite JGBs rally.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen off in late trade despite JGBs rally.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures backed off slightly from their recent euphoric highs in late Monday trade as the market took a breather amid a lack of fresh news.
"The market has priced in quite a lot already. It's difficult for it to go higher and there was no news today," said a trader with an Asian futures house.
He said June Euroyen would face strong resistance at 99.33 unless there were comments from Japanese officials indicating the economy was slowing down.
The lead June Euroyen contract stood at 99.26 in late trade against its IMM close at 99.28, after touching its contract high of 99.30 early in the day. Volume was a low 5,820 lots.
Japanese government bond (JGB) futures for December settled at 124.64 against their opening 124.70, after shooting to a new high of 124.96.

"It's been incredible. They've been making new highs every day," said the trader, adding that Monday's rally was largely technically-driven. "Some programme buys came in when it broke through 124.85, taking it straight to 124.95/96."
He said December JGBs would face a further barrier at 125.15/20 but added: "Bonds are probably due for a correction. This is quite an unwarranted move."

The already bullish JGBs received an added boost last week on news Japan's Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau would maintain its portfolio strategy, which is heavily weighted towards government bonds.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly firmer in quiet trade ahead of a slew of U.S. economic data later this week.
The most active March contract finished at 94.32 against its IMM close at 94.31.
Dealers said the market was eagerly awaiting the release of U.S. third quarter employment cost index and gross domestic product due on Tuesday and Wednesday, respectively.
